newsitem.title: INDIA: Enron unit to seal India LNG sales. [CORRECTED 15:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Enron unit to seal India LNG sales. [CORRECTED 15:10 GMT]

text.p: Enron India Natural Gas Inc, a subsidiary of U.S. firm Enron Corp, will finalise the sale of surplus liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Indian power and fertiliser units within two weeks, a company official said on Monday.

The official, who did not want to be identified, told Reuters that the sale of the gas from Qatar, which would be left over after use in its power plant at Dabhol, would be restricted to two western Indian states.
"The LNG sale will be restricted to projects located in Gujarat and Maharashtra. We expect to sign a memorandum of understanding with six or seven buyers within a fortnight," he said.
In 1995 Enron signed an agreement with the Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC) to produce five million tonnes of LNG every year from 2001.
It proposed to ship 2.0 million tonnes of LNG to feed its 2,500 megawatt (corrects from 2,184 megawatt) power project being built at Dabhol on the Arabian Sea coast in Maharashtra.

However, last September, Enron, which was aiming to supply the remaining 2.0 million tonnes (corrects from 3.0 million tonnes) to Israel, lost an expected supply contract and was forced to earmark its entire output to Indian fertiliser and power plants facing fuel shortages.
The surplus arising from the change will amount to 12 million cubic metres of gas per day.
"So far, demand expressed by project promoters (in India) has touched 110 million cubic metres (per day)," the Enron official said.
"The overwhelming response has forced us to limit LNG supply initially to Maharashtra and Gujarat. Other states will be considered as and when Enron signs a new export agreement with QGPC," he said.

The official said export to India could be revised once a planned rise in output from Qatar's third LNG project was realised. Enron's proposed $5 billion project in Qatar will be known as Qatar-Enron Marketing Company.
QGPC and Enron hold 65 percent and 35 percent, respectively, in the company.

(Corrects to remove reference to gas field involving Enron, called the "Enron Project". Also deletes reference to field's estimated output.) "Enron and QGPC will be reviewing the amount of LNG export to India once the revised projections are established," the official said.
